startup.name: Fed10
startup.description: Legislative consulting staffed by AI agents: monitors every bill in the US, flags business threats and delivers insights like a policy consultant. Three founders who are former lobbyists. Team of 3 in San Francisco.

yc_acceptance.basis: The company is already in the batch that starts at the as_of date, so the acceptance step is reported only for completeness: the prior for a random applicant is about 1 percent (0.6 to 2 percent), and conditional on being accepted the forecast below is what matters. Three founders with direct lobbying experience give founder market fit; the market is niche and a services style pitch can read as small.
yc_acceptance.why_it_fails: YC would most plausibly say no because government affairs is a small market with entrenched tools such as Quorum and FiscalNote, the consulting framing suggests services margins, and AI summaries of bills are easy to copy. Three ex lobbyists give strong founder market fit, which is the main thing that would carry the interview, but the question of venture scale would be pointed.

ladder.why_it_fails: Window of 10.4 months (2026-01-05 to 2026-11-17). Government affairs software is a mature niche led by Quorum and FiscalNote, with Plural and others, and the buyer pool of corporate government relations teams is small. GovPredict was acquired after a seed and Parsagon and Axis, close analogs, never raised past it, so a round above $1M within 10 months depends on proving paid users beyond the founders' network.

Strong Series A of $20M to $40M for a fast growing product with revenue. Series A bands use the 2022+ YC table (p25 $11M, median $15M, p75 $21M) and public medians of about $17M.

ladder.why_it_fails: A Series A within 10 months is very unlikely: the buyer pool of corporate government relations teams and trade associations is small, buyers are conservative and slow, and a three person team would need over $1M of ARR. Incumbents that already track bills now market AI agents, and no analog in legislative tracking in the data has reached Series A, so the cohort shows no precedent for it.

The narrow market makes that expansion rare, the analogs GovPredict, Parsagon and Axis never got near it, and nothing in this short window suggests the company gets there.

ladder.why_it_fails: Series C needs a platform sized government relations business with large multi year contracts, and the category has produced few venture scale outcomes. GovPredict was acquired at small scale, FiscalNote is a public incumbent that has struggled, and almost no company reaches this stage in the 10 month window, so the probability is a floor value only.

outcomes.why_it_fails: The most likely end is a stall or a small acquisition by Quorum, FiscalNote, Plural or a law firm, as happened to GovPredict. A venture sized outcome requires turning the consulting wedge into software that expands beyond lobbying into regulatory compliance and agency rules, and the founders must prove that corporate buyers pay for AI analysis rather than for the people who relay it.

technical_complexity.rationale: Ingesting every federal and state bill and producing relevant, accurate threat analysis is within reach for a small team with LLMs; the hard parts are coverage, accuracy and tailoring to each client's business. Not a deep technical moat.

narrative.headline: Strong founder fit in a small, incumbent held niche; 10 month seed odds are below the ever anchor.
narrative.general_summary: Fed10 is a legislative consulting firm staffed by AI agents, run by three former lobbyists. In a 10.4 month window the B2B cohort anchor of 0.61 for ever reaching seed shrinks to about 0.38, because most seeds arrive later than that. Series A inside the window is about 0.04. Quorum and FiscalNote already sell AI bill tracking, and close analogs such as GovPredict, Parsagon and Axis stayed small or exited low. Founder market fit helps, but the odds here do not rank this company against others.

assumptions: Blind forecast made as of 2026-01-05 using only the YC batch description in the input file, with market-only web searches.
Forecast window is 10.4 months, from 2026-01-05 to 2026-11-17.

Seed means an outside financing round above about $1M that closes inside the window, not the standard YC deal of about $500K; the seed and Series A probabilities are window probabilities, not ever probabilities.

The odds do not rank this company against other companies in the batch: in the 2026 winners test, team size, claimed traction and a hot sector did not separate raisers from non raisers, so the seed number stays near the cohort anchor.
Cohort anchors come from older and 2022 to 2024 batches and are partly right censored; funding coverage in the data is incomplete (lower, known and upper ranges quoted).
